ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the right triangle $ABC$, where $\angle C=90^\circ$, the bisector of $\angle ABC$, $BD$, intersects $AC$ at $D$. If $CD = 4\, \text{cm}$, what is the distance from point $D$ to $AB$, denoted as $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle C=90^\circ$ and BD bisects $\angle ABC$, with $DE \perp AB$,\\
it follows that $DE=CD$,\\
Since $CD=4\text{cm}$,\\
the distance from point D to AB, DE, is $\boxed{4\text{cm}}$.

First read the figure: triangle ABC is right-angled at C, D lies on side AC, BD is drawn from B to D, E lies on AB, and DE is the perpendicular distance from D to AB. From the text, BD bisects angle ABC and CD = 4 cm. Since D is on the angle bisector of angle ABC, its perpendicular distances to the two sides BA and BC of that angle are equal. The distance from D to BA is DE. Because AC is perpendicular to BC and D lies on AC, the perpendicular distance from D to BC is CD. Therefore DE = CD = 4 cm.
